helmet.meaning: A helmet protects a worker’s head on site.
helmet.definition: A helmet protects a worker’s head on site.
helmet.example: Always wear your helmet before entering the work area.

panel.meaning: A panel contains switches and electrical control equipment.
panel.definition: A panel contains switches and electrical control equipment.
panel.example: Did you check the panel door before starting the inspection?

switch.meaning: A switch turns electrical equipment on or off.
switch.definition: A switch turns electrical equipment on or off.
switch.example: Make sure the main switch is off before any maintenance work.

drawing.meaning: A drawing shows the size and position of engineering work.
drawing.definition: A drawing shows the size and position of engineering work.
drawing.example: If the drawing had been reviewed earlier, the error could have been prevented.

inspect.meaning: To inspect means to check work or equipment carefully.
inspect.definition: To inspect means to check work or equipment carefully.
inspect.example: Please inspect the electrical panel thoroughly this morning.

cable tray.meaning: A cable tray is a metal or plastic support system used to route, support, and protect electrical cables along walls, ceilings, and floors.
cable tray.definition: A cable tray is a metal or plastic support system used to route, support, and protect electrical cables along walls, ceilings, and floors.
cable tray.example: Verify the cable tray installation before proceeding to the next phase.

support.meaning: A support holds equipment or containment in the correct position.
support.definition: A support holds equipment or containment in the correct position.
support.example: Always check that the support spacing meets the specification requirements.

complete.meaning: Complete means that all required work is finished.
complete.definition: Complete means that all required work is finished.
complete.example: Is the cable tray work complete and ready for inspection?

inspection request.meaning: An inspection request is a formal request submitted to the responsible team or consultant to check and verify completed work before proceeding.
inspection request.definition: An inspection request is a formal request submitted to the responsible team or consultant to check and verify completed work before proceeding.
inspection request.example: Please submit the inspection request before the next work front opens.

work area.meaning: A work area is the defined place where a team performs an activity.
work area.definition: A work area is the defined place where a team performs an activity.
work area.example: Keep the work area clean and safe during all installation activities.

transformer.meaning: A transformer transfers electrical energy between circuits and raises or lowers voltage for safe distribution.
transformer.definition: A transformer transfers electrical energy between circuits and raises or lowers voltage for safe distribution.
transformer.example: If the transformer oil temperature exceeds the limit, shutdown must be initiated immediately.

switchgear.meaning: Switchgear is a group of breakers, isolators, relays, and panels used to control electrical power safely.
switchgear.definition: Switchgear is a group of breakers, isolators, relays, and panels used to control electrical power safely.
switchgear.example: Did the contractor submit the switchgear test certificates on time?

busbar.meaning: A busbar is a rigid conductor that distributes high current within switchboards or distribution boards.
busbar.definition: A busbar is a rigid conductor that distributes high current within switchboards or distribution boards.
busbar.example: Make sure the busbar torque values are verified before energizing the panel.

circuit breaker.meaning: A circuit breaker automatically opens an electrical circuit when it detects overload or fault current.
circuit breaker.definition: A circuit breaker automatically opens an electrical circuit when it detects overload or fault current.
circuit breaker.example: Always confirm the circuit breaker is in the OFF position before commencing work.

relay.meaning: A relay detects abnormal electrical conditions and sends a signal to trip or control equipment.
relay.definition: A relay detects abnormal electrical conditions and sends a signal to trip or control equipment.
relay.example: If the protection relay trips, investigate the root cause before resetting.

earthing.meaning: Earthing provides a low-resistance path for fault current to protect people and equipment.
earthing.definition: Earthing provides a low-resistance path for fault current to protect people and equipment.
earthing.example: Verify the earthing conductor is properly bonded before the system goes live.

insulation resistance.meaning: Insulation resistance indicates how well cable or equipment insulation prevents leakage current.
insulation resistance.definition: Insulation resistance indicates how well cable or equipment insulation prevents leakage current.
insulation resistance.example: The cable passed the insulation resistance test at one kilovolt.

short circuit.meaning: A short circuit occurs when current flows through an unintended path with very low resistance.
short circuit.definition: A short circuit occurs when current flows through an unintended path with very low resistance.
short circuit.example: The report identified a short circuit between the control cores inside the junction box.

load flow.meaning: Load flow analysis calculates voltage, current, power, and losses in an electrical network.
load flow.definition: Load flow analysis calculates voltage, current, power, and losses in an electrical network.
load flow.example: The consultant requested a revised load flow study after the chiller load increased.

selectivity.meaning: Selectivity ensures the protective device nearest to a fault trips before upstream devices.
selectivity.definition: Selectivity ensures the protective device nearest to a fault trips before upstream devices.
selectivity.example: The protection engineer adjusted the breaker curves to improve selectivity.

harmonics.meaning: Harmonics are unwanted frequency components that distort voltage or current waveforms.
harmonics.definition: Harmonics are unwanted frequency components that distort voltage or current waveforms.
harmonics.example: The data center added harmonic filters after the UPS caused distortion on the LV board.

voltage drop.meaning: Voltage drop is the reduction in voltage between the source and the load caused by conductor impedance.
voltage drop.definition: Voltage drop is the reduction in voltage between the source and the load caused by conductor impedance.
voltage drop.example: The feeder size was increased because the calculated voltage drop exceeded the specification.

feeder.meaning: A feeder is a cable or circuit that supplies power from a source to equipment or a distribution board.
feeder.definition: A feeder is a cable or circuit that supplies power from a source to equipment or a distribution board.
feeder.example: The site team labelled each feeder before terminating it inside the MCC.

termination.meaning: Termination is the prepared connection of a cable core to equipment, terminals, or accessories.
termination.definition: Termination is the prepared connection of a cable core to equipment, terminals, or accessories.
termination.example: QA asked for photos of each cable termination before closing the panel covers.

conduit.meaning: A conduit protects electrical wiring and provides a defined route through walls or slabs.
conduit.definition: A conduit protects electrical wiring and provides a defined route through walls or slabs.
conduit.example: The architect asked the team to conceal the conduit inside the partition.

isolation.meaning: Isolation means separating equipment from its energy source before inspection or maintenance.
isolation.definition: Isolation means separating equipment from its energy source before inspection or maintenance.
isolation.example: The technician confirmed electrical isolation before opening the motor terminal box.

energize.meaning: To energize equipment is to connect it to a live electrical supply.
energize.definition: To energize equipment is to connect it to a live electrical supply.
energize.example: The client allowed the team to energize the panel after all pre-commissioning checks were signed.

nameplate rating.meaning: A nameplate rating is the official capacity or electrical value printed on equipment by the manufacturer.
nameplate rating.definition: A nameplate rating is the official capacity or electrical value printed on equipment by the manufacturer.
nameplate rating.example: The inspector compared the installed motor with the nameplate rating in the approved submittal.

single-line diagram.meaning: A single-line diagram represents a power system using one line for each circuit path.
single-line diagram.definition: A single-line diagram represents a power system using one line for each circuit path.
single-line diagram.example: The consultant marked the single-line diagram to show the revised generator connection.

chiller.meaning: A chiller removes heat from water so it can be circulated through an HVAC cooling system.
chiller.definition: A chiller removes heat from water so it can be circulated through an HVAC cooling system.
chiller.example: The commissioning engineer checked the chiller flow rate before starting the performance test.

pump.meaning: A pump moves water or another fluid through pipes by creating pressure and flow.
pump.definition: A pump moves water or another fluid through pipes by creating pressure and flow.
pump.example: The maintenance team aligned the pump before connecting it to the chilled water line.

valve.meaning: A valve opens, closes, or regulates the flow of liquid, gas, or air in a system.
valve.definition: A valve opens, closes, or regulates the flow of liquid, gas, or air in a system.
valve.example: The supervisor asked for the valve tag number before approving the shutdown.

actuator.meaning: An actuator converts a control signal into mechanical movement.
actuator.definition: An actuator converts a control signal into mechanical movement.
actuator.example: The BMS contractor replaced the actuator because the damper was not responding.

damper.meaning: A damper regulates or stops airflow inside ductwork.
damper.definition: A damper regulates or stops airflow inside ductwork.
damper.example: If the damper fails the test, corrective action is required.

ductwork.meaning: Ductwork carries supply, return, or exhaust air through a building.
ductwork.definition: Ductwork carries supply, return, or exhaust air through a building.
ductwork.example: The ductwork route was revised to clear the cable tray above the corridor.

static pressure.meaning: Static pressure is the pressure in a duct system that the fan must overcome to move air.
static pressure.definition: Static pressure is the pressure in a duct system that the fan must overcome to move air.
static pressure.example: The TAB report showed high static pressure across the filter section.

flow rate.meaning: Flow rate is the volume of fluid passing through a point during a specific time period.
flow rate.definition: Flow rate is the volume of fluid passing through a point during a specific time period.
flow rate.example: The consultant rejected the test because the chilled water flow rate was below design.

pressure drop.meaning: Pressure drop is the reduction in pressure as fluid or air passes through equipment, pipework, or filters.
pressure drop.definition: Pressure drop is the reduction in pressure as fluid or air passes through equipment, pipework, or filters.
pressure drop.example: The engineer calculated the pressure drop across the heat exchanger before selecting the pump.

heat exchanger.meaning: A heat exchanger transfers heat between two fluids without mixing them.
heat exchanger.definition: A heat exchanger transfers heat between two fluids without mixing them.
heat exchanger.example: Always verify the heat exchanger before proceeding.

bearing.meaning: A bearing supports a rotating shaft and reduces friction during operation.
bearing.definition: A bearing supports a rotating shaft and reduces friction during operation.
bearing.example: The vibration report suggested damage to the fan bearing.

vibration.meaning: Vibration is repeated movement that can indicate imbalance, misalignment, or mechanical wear.
vibration.definition: Vibration is repeated movement that can indicate imbalance, misalignment, or mechanical wear.
vibration.example: Make sure the vibration meets the specification.

torque.meaning: Torque is a rotational force applied to tighten, drive, or rotate a component.
torque.definition: Torque is a rotational force applied to tighten, drive, or rotate a component.
torque.example: The technician used a calibrated wrench to apply the specified torque to the flange bolts.

alignment.meaning: Alignment ensures shafts, couplings, or components are positioned correctly to avoid stress and wear.
alignment.definition: Alignment ensures shafts, couplings, or components are positioned correctly to avoid stress and wear.
alignment.example: The pump alignment record was attached to the mechanical completion dossier.

balancing.meaning: Balancing reduces uneven forces in rotating equipment or distributes air/water flow to design values.
balancing.definition: Balancing reduces uneven forces in rotating equipment or distributes air/water flow to design values.
balancing.example: The fan required balancing after the vibration test failed.

flange.meaning: A flange is a flat rim that allows pipes, valves, and equipment to be bolted together.
flange.definition: A flange is a flat rim that allows pipes, valves, and equipment to be bolted together.
flange.example: The QA inspector found a damaged gasket between the two flanges.

gasket.meaning: A gasket is a sealing material placed between flanges or joints to prevent leakage.
gasket.definition: A gasket is a sealing material placed between flanges or joints to prevent leakage.
gasket.example: The pressure test failed because the gasket was not seated correctly.

calibration.meaning: Calibration compares and adjusts instruments so their readings match an accepted reference.
calibration.definition: Calibration compares and adjusts instruments so their readings match an accepted reference.
calibration.example: If the calibration fails the test, corrective action is required.

thermal expansion.meaning: Thermal expansion is the increase in length or volume of a material as temperature rises.
thermal expansion.definition: Thermal expansion is the increase in length or volume of a material as temperature rises.
thermal expansion.example: The pipe supports were revised to allow thermal expansion during operation.

preventive maintenance.meaning: Preventive maintenance is scheduled work carried out to reduce the chance of equipment failure.
preventive maintenance.definition: Preventive maintenance is scheduled work carried out to reduce the chance of equipment failure.
preventive maintenance.example: The facilities team added the pumps to the preventive maintenance plan.

rebar.meaning: Rebar is steel reinforcement placed inside concrete to improve tensile strength.
rebar.definition: Rebar is steel reinforcement placed inside concrete to improve tensile strength.
rebar.example: The inspector checked the rebar spacing before allowing the concrete pour.

formwork.meaning: Formwork is a temporary structure that holds fresh concrete until it gains strength.
formwork.definition: Formwork is a temporary structure that holds fresh concrete until it gains strength.
formwork.example: The formwork was inspected before the slab was poured.

footing.meaning: A footing transfers building loads from columns or walls into the ground.
footing.definition: A footing transfers building loads from columns or walls into the ground.
footing.example: The footing depth was increased after the soil report identified weaker material.

slab.meaning: A slab is a flat horizontal concrete element used for floors, roofs, or foundations.
slab.definition: A slab is a flat horizontal concrete element used for floors, roofs, or foundations.
slab.example: The MEP team marked sleeve locations before casting the slab.

column.meaning: A column carries loads from beams or slabs down to foundations.
column.definition: A column carries loads from beams or slabs down to foundations.
column.example: The structural engineer asked for a survey check on the column position.

beam.meaning: A beam supports loads and transfers them to columns, walls, or other supports.
beam.definition: A beam supports loads and transfers them to columns, walls, or other supports.
beam.example: The contractor could not core through the beam without structural approval.

shear wall.meaning: A shear wall is a structural wall designed to resist wind or seismic lateral loads.
shear wall.definition: A shear wall is a structural wall designed to resist wind or seismic lateral loads.
shear wall.example: The architect coordinated door openings around the shear wall locations.

settlement.meaning: Settlement is the downward movement of soil or a structure due to loading or ground changes.
settlement.definition: Settlement is the downward movement of soil or a structure due to loading or ground changes.
settlement.example: The monitoring report showed minor settlement near the excavation boundary.

compaction.meaning: Compaction increases soil density to improve bearing capacity and reduce future settlement.
compaction.definition: Compaction increases soil density to improve bearing capacity and reduce future settlement.
compaction.example: When the compaction is checked, the inspector should document the findings.

curing.meaning: Curing maintains moisture and temperature so concrete can develop strength properly.
curing.definition: Curing maintains moisture and temperature so concrete can develop strength properly.
curing.example: The site team covered the slab for curing immediately after finishing.

aggregate.meaning: Aggregate is sand, gravel, or crushed stone used in concrete or road construction.
aggregate.definition: Aggregate is sand, gravel, or crushed stone used in concrete or road construction.
aggregate.example: The concrete mix was rejected because the aggregate grading did not match the approved design.

bearing capacity.meaning: Bearing capacity is the maximum pressure soil can safely support from a foundation.
bearing capacity.definition: Bearing capacity is the maximum pressure soil can safely support from a foundation.
bearing capacity.example: The geotechnical report confirmed adequate bearing capacity for shallow footings.

retaining wall.meaning: A retaining wall supports soil at different levels and prevents collapse or movement.
retaining wall.definition: A retaining wall supports soil at different levels and prevents collapse or movement.
retaining wall.example: The retaining wall drainage detail was revised after the design review.

punch list.meaning: A punch list records remaining defects or incomplete items before handover.
punch list.definition: A punch list records remaining defects or incomplete items before handover.
punch list.example: The client refused handover until the punch list items were closed.

method statement.meaning: A method statement describes the sequence, resources, risks, and controls for a construction activity.
method statement.definition: A method statement describes the sequence, resources, risks, and controls for a construction activity.
method statement.example: Please review the method statement before commencing the activity.

shop drawing.meaning: A shop drawing shows how approved design information will be fabricated, assembled, or installed.
shop drawing.definition: A shop drawing shows how approved design information will be fabricated, assembled, or installed.
shop drawing.example: The site team could not proceed because the shop drawing was still under review.

as-built drawing.meaning: An as-built drawing records the actual installed arrangement after construction changes.
as-built drawing.definition: An as-built drawing records the actual installed arrangement after construction changes.
as-built drawing.example: Please submit the as-built drawing after completing the installation work.

site instruction.meaning: A site instruction directs a contractor to carry out, change, or correct work.
site instruction.definition: A site instruction directs a contractor to carry out, change, or correct work.
site instruction.example: The contractor requested a cost assessment after receiving the site instruction.

workfront.meaning: A workfront is an area or scope where a crew can start or continue work.
workfront.definition: A workfront is an area or scope where a crew can start or continue work.
workfront.example: The planner reported that the electrical team had no clear workfront on level three.

access constraint.meaning: An access constraint is a limitation that prevents people, materials, or equipment from reaching a work area.
access constraint.definition: An access constraint is a limitation that prevents people, materials, or equipment from reaching a work area.
access constraint.example: The crane delivery was delayed due to an access constraint at the service road.

facade.meaning: A facade is the visible external face or envelope of a building.
facade.definition: A facade is the visible external face or envelope of a building.
facade.example: The facade contractor coordinated bracket locations with the structural engineer.

atrium.meaning: An atrium is a tall open space inside a building, often connecting several floors.
atrium.definition: An atrium is a tall open space inside a building, often connecting several floors.
atrium.example: The smoke control strategy was reviewed because the atrium connects five levels.

partition.meaning: A partition divides interior spaces without usually carrying structural loads.
partition.definition: A partition divides interior spaces without usually carrying structural loads.
partition.example: The electrical sockets were relocated after the partition layout changed.

egress.meaning: Egress is the route people use to leave a building safely during normal use or an emergency.
egress.definition: Egress is the route people use to leave a building safely during normal use or an emergency.
egress.example: Has the emergency egress been inspected during the safety walkdown?

building envelope.meaning: The building envelope includes walls, roof, glazing, and insulation that protect interior spaces.
building envelope.definition: The building envelope includes walls, roof, glazing, and insulation that protect interior spaces.
building envelope.example: The design review focused on air leakage through the building envelope.

louver.meaning: A louver is a set of angled slats that allows airflow while limiting rain, views, or debris.
louver.definition: A louver is a set of angled slats that allows airflow while limiting rain, views, or debris.
louver.example: The generator room louver size was increased to meet ventilation requirements.

ceiling void.meaning: A ceiling void is the concealed space above ceiling panels where services often run.
ceiling void.definition: A ceiling void is the concealed space above ceiling panels where services often run.
ceiling void.example: The ceiling void was too shallow for the duct and cable tray crossing.

finish schedule.meaning: A finish schedule lists floor, wall, ceiling, and other surface finishes for each space.
finish schedule.definition: A finish schedule lists floor, wall, ceiling, and other surface finishes for each space.
finish schedule.example: Procurement used the finish schedule to confirm tile quantities.

baseline programme.meaning: A baseline programme is the approved project schedule used to measure progress and delays.
baseline programme.definition: A baseline programme is the approved project schedule used to measure progress and delays.
baseline programme.example: The planner compared actual progress against the baseline programme in the weekly report.

milestone.meaning: A milestone is a key date or deliverable used to track project progress.
milestone.definition: A milestone is a key date or deliverable used to track project progress.
milestone.example: Factory acceptance testing became a critical milestone for the switchgear package.

critical path.meaning: The critical path is the longest sequence of dependent activities that determines the project completion date.
critical path.definition: The critical path is the longest sequence of dependent activities that determines the project completion date.
critical path.example: The delay to transformer delivery affected the critical path.

float.meaning: Float is available time before an activity delay affects a milestone or completion date.
float.definition: Float is available time before an activity delay affects a milestone or completion date.
float.example: The planner warned that the cable pulling activity had no remaining float.

risk register.meaning: A risk register records risks, owners, probability, impact, and mitigation actions.
risk register.definition: A risk register records risks, owners, probability, impact, and mitigation actions.
risk register.example: The project manager added late authority approval to the risk register.

variation order.meaning: A variation order formally changes the contract scope, value, or time.
variation order.definition: A variation order formally changes the contract scope, value, or time.
variation order.example: The contractor submitted a variation order for the additional cable route.

procurement schedule.meaning: A procurement schedule tracks submittals, approvals, manufacturing, delivery, and site need dates.
procurement schedule.definition: A procurement schedule tracks submittals, approvals, manufacturing, delivery, and site need dates.
procurement schedule.example: The procurement schedule showed that the pumps would arrive after the planned installation date.

stakeholder.meaning: A stakeholder is anyone with an interest in or influence over a project.
stakeholder.definition: A stakeholder is anyone with an interest in or influence over a project.
stakeholder.example: The project team mapped stakeholders before changing the road closure plan.

permit to work.meaning: A permit to work authorizes hazardous or controlled activities after risks and controls are reviewed.
permit to work.definition: A permit to work authorizes hazardous or controlled activities after risks and controls are reviewed.
permit to work.example: The supervisor refused to start hot work without a valid permit to work.

toolbox talk.meaning: A toolbox talk is a short site briefing about hazards, controls, and safe work methods.
toolbox talk.definition: A toolbox talk is a short site briefing about hazards, controls, and safe work methods.
toolbox talk.example: The safety officer gave a toolbox talk before the confined space entry.

lockout-tagout.meaning: Lockout-tagout is a safety procedure that isolates energy and identifies who controls the lock.
lockout-tagout.definition: Lockout-tagout is a safety procedure that isolates energy and identifies who controls the lock.
lockout-tagout.example: The technician applied lockout-tagout before servicing the pump starter.

hazard.meaning: A hazard is anything that can cause injury, illness, damage, or loss.
hazard.definition: A hazard is anything that can cause injury, illness, damage, or loss.
hazard.example: Loose materials near the stairwell were reported as a trip hazard.

risk assessment.meaning: A risk assessment identifies hazards, estimates risk, and defines control measures.
risk assessment.definition: A risk assessment identifies hazards, estimates risk, and defines control measures.
risk assessment.example: Make sure the risk assessment is completed before starting any high-risk work.

near miss.meaning: A near miss is an unplanned event that did not cause injury but had the potential to do so.
near miss.definition: A near miss is an unplanned event that did not cause injury but had the potential to do so.
near miss.example: The falling bolt was recorded as a near miss and discussed in the safety meeting.

PPE.meaning: PPE is equipment worn to reduce exposure to workplace hazards.
PPE.definition: PPE is equipment worn to reduce exposure to workplace hazards.
PPE.example: Visitors were not allowed on site without the required PPE.

confined space.meaning: A confined space is an enclosed or partly enclosed area with limited access and potential atmospheric hazards.
confined space.definition: A confined space is an enclosed or partly enclosed area with limited access and potential atmospheric hazards.
confined space.example: The tank was treated as a confined space and required gas testing before entry.

pre-commissioning.meaning: Pre-commissioning includes inspections and static checks completed before systems are operated.
pre-commissioning.definition: Pre-commissioning includes inspections and static checks completed before systems are operated.
pre-commissioning.example: The team completed pre-commissioning checks before starting the chilled water pumps.

functional test.meaning: A functional test verifies that equipment or a system operates as designed.
functional test.definition: A functional test verifies that equipment or a system operates as designed.
functional test.example: The fire alarm functional test confirmed that the AHU shut down correctly.

integrated systems test.meaning: An integrated systems test verifies interfaces between systems during a realistic scenario.
integrated systems test.definition: An integrated systems test verifies interfaces between systems during a realistic scenario.
integrated systems test.example: The integrated systems test checked fire alarm, lifts, smoke fans, and access control together.

witness test.meaning: A witness test is performed while an authorized party observes and accepts the result.
witness test.definition: A witness test is performed while an authorized party observes and accepts the result.
witness test.example: The consultant attended the witness test for the generator load bank.

snagging.meaning: Snagging is the process of identifying incomplete or defective work before acceptance.
snagging.definition: Snagging is the process of identifying incomplete or defective work before acceptance.
snagging.example: The commissioning manager scheduled snagging after the final room inspection.

handover dossier.meaning: A handover dossier contains approved records, test results, manuals, certificates, and as-built information.
handover dossier.definition: A handover dossier contains approved records, test results, manuals, certificates, and as-built information.
handover dossier.example: The client would not accept the plantroom without a complete handover dossier.

O&M manual.meaning: An O&M manual explains how to operate, maintain, and troubleshoot installed equipment or systems.
O&M manual.definition: An O&M manual explains how to operate, maintain, and troubleshoot installed equipment or systems.
O&M manual.example: Facilities asked for the O&M manual before taking over the booster pump set.

seasonal commissioning.meaning: Seasonal commissioning verifies system performance under conditions not available at initial handover.
seasonal commissioning.definition: Seasonal commissioning verifies system performance under conditions not available at initial handover.
seasonal commissioning.example: The cooling system required seasonal commissioning during peak summer load.

factory acceptance test.meaning: A factory acceptance test verifies equipment at the factory before shipment to site.
factory acceptance test.definition: A factory acceptance test verifies equipment at the factory before shipment to site.
factory acceptance test.example: The client attended the factory acceptance test for the LV switchboard.

site acceptance test.meaning: A site acceptance test verifies equipment after installation at the project site.
site acceptance test.definition: A site acceptance test verifies equipment after installation at the project site.
site acceptance test.example: The UPS passed the site acceptance test after battery autonomy was confirmed.

pressure test.meaning: A pressure test verifies that pipework or vessels can hold pressure without leakage.
pressure test.definition: A pressure test verifies that pipework or vessels can hold pressure without leakage.
pressure test.example: The chilled water pipe failed the pressure test at the valve flange.

load bank test.meaning: A load bank test applies controlled load to a generator or UPS to verify performance.
load bank test.definition: A load bank test applies controlled load to a generator or UPS to verify performance.
load bank test.example: The generator completed a four-hour load bank test at eighty percent load.

continuity test.meaning: A continuity test checks whether a conductor or circuit path is complete.
continuity test.definition: A continuity test checks whether a conductor or circuit path is complete.
continuity test.example: The technician performed a continuity test on each control cable core.

calibrated instrument.meaning: A calibrated instrument has been checked against a standard and is suitable for reliable measurement.
calibrated instrument.definition: A calibrated instrument has been checked against a standard and is suitable for reliable measurement.
calibrated instrument.example: QA rejected the reading because the pressure gauge calibration certificate had expired.

test certificate.meaning: A test certificate records that a test was completed and states the accepted result.
test certificate.definition: A test certificate records that a test was completed and states the accepted result.
test certificate.example: The handover file was missing the fire pump test certificate.

acceptance criteria.meaning: Acceptance criteria define the conditions that must be met for a test or deliverable to be accepted.
acceptance criteria.definition: Acceptance criteria define the conditions that must be met for a test or deliverable to be accepted.
acceptance criteria.example: Make sure the acceptance criteria are clearly defined before testing begins.

rack.meaning: A rack is a cabinet or frame used to mount servers, switches, and patch panels.
rack.definition: A rack is a cabinet or frame used to mount servers, switches, and patch panels.
rack.example: The network team reserved two racks for the new storage equipment.

hot aisle.meaning: A hot aisle is the row space where server racks discharge warm exhaust air.
hot aisle.definition: A hot aisle is the row space where server racks discharge warm exhaust air.
hot aisle.example: Containment panels were added above the hot aisle to improve cooling efficiency.

cold aisle.meaning: A cold aisle is the row space where servers receive chilled supply air.
cold aisle.definition: A cold aisle is the row space where servers receive chilled supply air.
cold aisle.example: The operator found blocked floor grilles in the cold aisle during inspection.

PUE.meaning: PUE measures total facility energy divided by IT equipment energy.
PUE.definition: PUE measures total facility energy divided by IT equipment energy.
PUE.example: The client asked for a lower PUE target during the sustainability review.

redundancy.meaning: Redundancy provides backup equipment or paths so service continues after a failure.
redundancy.definition: Redundancy provides backup equipment or paths so service continues after a failure.
redundancy.example: The design provides N+1 redundancy for the cooling plant.

UPS.meaning: A UPS provides temporary power when the main electrical supply fails or fluctuates.
UPS.definition: A UPS provides temporary power when the main electrical supply fails or fluctuates.
UPS.example: The UPS alarm was investigated before the planned shutdown.

CRAC unit.meaning: A CRAC unit controls temperature and airflow in data center spaces.
CRAC unit.definition: A CRAC unit controls temperature and airflow in data center spaces.
CRAC unit.example: The CRAC unit filter alarm appeared during the weekly facilities check.

structured cabling.meaning: Structured cabling is a standardized cabling system for data, voice, and network services.
structured cabling.definition: Structured cabling is a standardized cabling system for data, voice, and network services.
structured cabling.example: The installer tested every structured cabling link before handover.

clarify.meaning: To clarify means to make a point, instruction, or requirement easier to understand.
clarify.definition: To clarify means to make a point, instruction, or requirement easier to understand.
clarify.example: The engineer asked the consultant to clarify the comment before revising the drawing.

confirm.meaning: To confirm means to verify or formally state that information is correct.
confirm.definition: To confirm means to verify or formally state that information is correct.
confirm.example: Please confirm whether the inspection can proceed tomorrow morning.

mitigate.meaning: To mitigate means to reduce risk, delay, damage, or negative impact.
mitigate.definition: To mitigate means to reduce risk, delay, damage, or negative impact.
mitigate.example: The team proposed night shifts to mitigate the schedule delay.

escalate.meaning: To escalate means to bring an issue to senior people because it cannot be solved at the current level.
escalate.definition: To escalate means to bring an issue to senior people because it cannot be solved at the current level.
escalate.example: The site manager escalated the access issue to the client representative.

deviation.meaning: A deviation is a departure from a specification, drawing, method, or approved requirement.
deviation.definition: A deviation is a departure from a specification, drawing, method, or approved requirement.
deviation.example: The QA report recorded a deviation from the approved cable tray route.

constraint.meaning: A constraint is a condition that limits what can be done, when, or how.
constraint.definition: A constraint is a condition that limits what can be done, when, or how.
constraint.example: The low ceiling height became a major coordination constraint.

deliverable.meaning: A deliverable is a document, drawing, system, or result that must be provided under a project agreement.
deliverable.definition: A deliverable is a document, drawing, system, or result that must be provided under a project agreement.
deliverable.example: The commissioning plan was listed as a key deliverable for this month.

action owner.meaning: An action owner is the person assigned to complete a task after a meeting or review.
action owner.definition: An action owner is the person assigned to complete a task after a meeting or review.
action owner.example: The minutes named the electrical lead as the action owner for the cable schedule.

minutes of meeting.meaning: Minutes of meeting record decisions, actions, owners, and important discussion points.
minutes of meeting.definition: Minutes of meeting record decisions, actions, owners, and important discussion points.
minutes of meeting.example: The project manager circulated the minutes of meeting within twenty-four hours.

agenda.meaning: An agenda is a planned list of topics to be discussed in a meeting.
agenda.definition: An agenda is a planned list of topics to be discussed in a meeting.
agenda.example: The chair added commissioning access to the agenda for the coordination meeting.

consensus.meaning: Consensus is a shared agreement reached by most or all stakeholders after discussion.
consensus.definition: Consensus is a shared agreement reached by most or all stakeholders after discussion.
consensus.example: The design team reached consensus on the revised plantroom layout.

load schedule.meaning: A load schedule lists equipment loads, demand factors, circuit references, and connected capacity.
load schedule.definition: A load schedule lists equipment loads, demand factors, circuit references, and connected capacity.
load schedule.example: The electrical engineer updated the load schedule after the tenant added kitchen equipment.

diversity factor.meaning: A diversity factor accounts for the fact that not all connected loads operate at full demand at the same time.
diversity factor.definition: A diversity factor accounts for the fact that not all connected loads operate at full demand at the same time.
diversity factor.example: The consultant challenged the diversity factor used for the residential distribution board.

fault current.meaning: Fault current is the abnormal current that flows when a short circuit or earth fault occurs.
fault current.definition: Fault current is the abnormal current that flows when a short circuit or earth fault occurs.
fault current.example: Make sure the fault current meets the specification.

arc flash.meaning: An arc flash is a high-energy electrical explosion caused by current passing through air.
arc flash.definition: An arc flash is a high-energy electrical explosion caused by current passing through air.
arc flash.example: The safety briefing explained arc flash boundaries before panel testing.

residual current device.meaning: A residual current device trips when leakage current suggests a shock or earth fault risk.
residual current device.definition: A residual current device trips when leakage current suggests a shock or earth fault risk.
residual current device.example: The RCD was tested at the temporary site distribution board.

surge protection.meaning: Surge protection limits transient overvoltage caused by lightning or switching events.
surge protection.definition: Surge protection limits transient overvoltage caused by lightning or switching events.
surge protection.example: The data rack panel included surge protection for sensitive network equipment.

power factor.meaning: Power factor indicates how effectively electrical power is converted into useful work.
power factor.definition: Power factor indicates how effectively electrical power is converted into useful work.
power factor.example: The utility required power factor correction for the large motor loads.

capacitor bank.meaning: A capacitor bank supplies reactive power to improve power factor and reduce electrical losses.
capacitor bank.definition: A capacitor bank supplies reactive power to improve power factor and reduce electrical losses.
capacitor bank.example: The capacitor bank was isolated after the protection relay alarm.

motor control center.meaning: A motor control center contains starters, protection, and controls for several motors.
motor control center.definition: A motor control center contains starters, protection, and controls for several motors.
motor control center.example: If the motor control center fails the test, corrective action is required.

variable frequency drive.meaning: A variable frequency drive controls motor speed by adjusting electrical frequency and voltage.
variable frequency drive.definition: A variable frequency drive controls motor speed by adjusting electrical frequency and voltage.
variable frequency drive.example: The VFD parameters were adjusted to reduce pump start-up pressure surges.

air handling unit.meaning: An air handling unit filters, heats, cools, or moves air through an HVAC system.
air handling unit.definition: An air handling unit filters, heats, cools, or moves air through an HVAC system.
air handling unit.example: The AHU access door was blocked by temporary materials during inspection.

fan coil unit.meaning: A fan coil unit uses a fan and coil to condition air in a room or zone.
fan coil unit.definition: A fan coil unit uses a fan and coil to condition air in a room or zone.
fan coil unit.example: The tenant complained that the fan coil unit above the office was noisy.

expansion vessel.meaning: An expansion vessel absorbs pressure changes caused by thermal expansion in a closed water system.
expansion vessel.definition: An expansion vessel absorbs pressure changes caused by thermal expansion in a closed water system.
expansion vessel.example: The pressure fluctuated because the expansion vessel had lost its charge.

strainer.meaning: A strainer removes debris from water or fluid before it reaches sensitive equipment.
strainer.definition: A strainer removes debris from water or fluid before it reaches sensitive equipment.
strainer.example: The commissioning team cleaned the strainer after flushing the chilled water loop.

flushing.meaning: Flushing removes debris, scale, and contaminants from pipework before operation.
flushing.definition: Flushing removes debris, scale, and contaminants from pipework before operation.
flushing.example: The consultant requested flushing records before approving pump start-up.

differential pressure.meaning: Differential pressure is the pressure difference measured across equipment, filters, or pipe sections.
differential pressure.definition: Differential pressure is the pressure difference measured across equipment, filters, or pipe sections.
differential pressure.example: The dirty filter alarm was triggered by high differential pressure.

condensate drain.meaning: A condensate drain carries water produced by cooling coils or air conditioning equipment.
condensate drain.definition: A condensate drain carries water produced by cooling coils or air conditioning equipment.
condensate drain.example: The ceiling leak came from a blocked condensate drain above the meeting room.

heat load.meaning: Heat load is the thermal demand used to size cooling or heating equipment.
heat load.definition: Heat load is the thermal demand used to size cooling or heating equipment.
heat load.example: Review the heat load before final approval.

fresh air rate.meaning: Fresh air rate is the quantity of outdoor air provided for ventilation and indoor air quality.
fresh air rate.definition: Fresh air rate is the quantity of outdoor air provided for ventilation and indoor air quality.
fresh air rate.example: The inspector checked the fresh air rate against the occupancy schedule.

acoustic lining.meaning: Acoustic lining reduces noise transmission in ducts, plantrooms, or enclosures.
acoustic lining.definition: Acoustic lining reduces noise transmission in ducts, plantrooms, or enclosures.
acoustic lining.example: The consultant requested acoustic lining near the generator exhaust path.

pile foundation.meaning: A pile foundation uses long structural elements to transfer loads to deeper, stronger ground.
pile foundation.definition: A pile foundation uses long structural elements to transfer loads to deeper, stronger ground.
pile foundation.example: The structural design changed to a pile foundation after weak soil was found.

pile cap.meaning: A pile cap connects piles and distributes column or wall loads into them.
pile cap.definition: A pile cap connects piles and distributes column or wall loads into them.
pile cap.example: The rebar congestion in the pile cap required a revised pouring sequence.

waterproofing membrane.meaning: A waterproofing membrane is a protective layer that stops water entering a structure.
waterproofing membrane.definition: A waterproofing membrane is a protective layer that stops water entering a structure.
waterproofing membrane.example: The basement waterproofing membrane was inspected before backfilling.

expansion joint.meaning: An expansion joint allows parts of a structure to move without cracking or damage.
expansion joint.definition: An expansion joint allows parts of a structure to move without cracking or damage.
expansion joint.example: The expansion joint cover was damaged near the entrance lobby.

deflection.meaning: Deflection is the movement or bending of a structural element under load.
deflection.definition: Deflection is the movement or bending of a structural element under load.
deflection.example: The beam deflection was within the allowable serviceability limit.

camber.meaning: Camber is a slight upward curve built into a member to offset expected deflection.
camber.definition: Camber is a slight upward curve built into a member to offset expected deflection.
camber.example: The steel beam was fabricated with camber as shown on the shop drawing.

screed.meaning: A screed is a floor layer used to create a smooth, level surface before finishes.
screed.definition: A screed is a floor layer used to create a smooth, level surface before finishes.
screed.example: The tiling could not start because the screed had not cured.

blockwork.meaning: Blockwork is wall construction using concrete, masonry, or lightweight blocks.
blockwork.definition: Blockwork is wall construction using concrete, masonry, or lightweight blocks.
blockwork.example: The electrical boxes were installed before the blockwork was plastered.

plastering.meaning: Plastering creates a smooth surface on walls or ceilings before painting or finishing.
plastering.definition: Plastering creates a smooth surface on walls or ceilings before painting or finishing.
plastering.example: The plastering crew repaired the wall after the conduit change.

grouting.meaning: Grouting fills joints, voids, or spaces around tiles, bases, anchors, or equipment.
grouting.definition: Grouting fills joints, voids, or spaces around tiles, bases, anchors, or equipment.
grouting.example: The pump base grouting was completed before final alignment.

mobilization.meaning: Mobilization is the process of bringing labor, equipment, materials, and facilities to site.
mobilization.definition: Mobilization is the process of bringing labor, equipment, materials, and facilities to site.
mobilization.example: The contractor planned mobilization immediately after receiving the letter of award.

demobilization.meaning: Demobilization is the removal of temporary facilities, equipment, and teams after completion.
demobilization.definition: Demobilization is the removal of temporary facilities, equipment, and teams after completion.
demobilization.example: Demobilization was delayed because several punch list items remained open.

material submittal.meaning: A material submittal provides product data, samples, and compliance information for approval.
material submittal.definition: A material submittal provides product data, samples, and compliance information for approval.
material submittal.example: The consultant rejected the material submittal because the cable tray coating was not specified.

mock-up.meaning: A mock-up is a sample of work built to confirm appearance, quality, and coordination before full installation.
mock-up.definition: A mock-up is a sample of work built to confirm appearance, quality, and coordination before full installation.
mock-up.example: The client approved the hotel room mock-up after reviewing finishes and lighting.

setback.meaning: A setback is the required distance between a building element and a property line, road, or other limit.
setback.definition: A setback is the required distance between a building element and a property line, road, or other limit.
setback.example: The balcony design was revised to comply with the setback requirement.

floor area ratio.meaning: Floor area ratio measures total building floor area compared with the site area.
floor area ratio.definition: Floor area ratio measures total building floor area compared with the site area.
floor area ratio.example: The developer reduced one floor to comply with the permitted floor area ratio.

accessibility.meaning: Accessibility means buildings can be used safely and comfortably by people with different mobility or sensory needs.
accessibility.definition: Accessibility means buildings can be used safely and comfortably by people with different mobility or sensory needs.
accessibility.example: The ramp gradient was changed to improve accessibility at the main entrance.

wayfinding.meaning: Wayfinding uses signs, layouts, landmarks, and visual cues to help people find routes.
wayfinding.definition: Wayfinding uses signs, layouts, landmarks, and visual cues to help people find routes.
wayfinding.example: The hospital lobby design improved wayfinding for visitors.

specification.meaning: A specification states required materials, workmanship, standards, and performance.
specification.definition: A specification states required materials, workmanship, standards, and performance.
specification.example: The contractor quoted an alternative pump that did not meet the specification.

scope gap.meaning: A scope gap occurs when required work is not clearly included in any party’s scope.
scope gap.definition: A scope gap occurs when required work is not clearly included in any party’s scope.
scope gap.example: The interface meeting identified a scope gap between the facade and steel contractors.

interface matrix.meaning: An interface matrix defines who is responsible for each connection, boundary, or dependency.
interface matrix.definition: An interface matrix defines who is responsible for each connection, boundary, or dependency.
interface matrix.example: The interface matrix clarified who would provide power to the BMS panels.

lookahead schedule.meaning: A lookahead schedule shows planned activities for the next few weeks in practical site detail.
lookahead schedule.definition: A lookahead schedule shows planned activities for the next few weeks in practical site detail.
lookahead schedule.example: The foreman used the three-week lookahead schedule to request materials.

earned value.meaning: Earned value compares planned work, actual cost, and completed work to assess project performance.
earned value.definition: Earned value compares planned work, actual cost, and completed work to assess project performance.
earned value.example: The controls report used earned value to show schedule slippage.

cash flow forecast.meaning: A cash flow forecast estimates project payments and expenditures over time.
cash flow forecast.definition: A cash flow forecast estimates project payments and expenditures over time.
cash flow forecast.example: Finance requested a revised cash flow forecast after the procurement delay.

lost time injury.meaning: A lost time injury is a work-related injury that prevents a person from returning to work for a defined period.
lost time injury.definition: A lost time injury is a work-related injury that prevents a person from returning to work for a defined period.
lost time injury.example: The monthly safety report recorded zero lost time injuries.

method of rescue.meaning: A method of rescue explains how workers will be safely recovered if an emergency occurs.
method of rescue.definition: A method of rescue explains how workers will be safely recovered if an emergency occurs.
method of rescue.example: When the method of rescue is checked, the inspector should document the findings.

exclusion zone.meaning: An exclusion zone keeps people away from hazards such as lifting, demolition, or energized work.
exclusion zone.definition: An exclusion zone keeps people away from hazards such as lifting, demolition, or energized work.
exclusion zone.example: The lifting supervisor set up an exclusion zone around the crane radius.

manual handling.meaning: Manual handling involves carrying, lifting, pushing, or pulling loads using physical effort.
manual handling.definition: Manual handling involves carrying, lifting, pushing, or pulling loads using physical effort.
manual handling.example: The toolbox talk covered manual handling techniques for moving cable drums.

scaffold tag.meaning: A scaffold tag indicates whether a scaffold is safe to use after inspection.
scaffold tag.definition: A scaffold tag indicates whether a scaffold is safe to use after inspection.
scaffold tag.example: Workers were told not to access the platform because the scaffold tag was missing.

hot work.meaning: Hot work includes welding, grinding, cutting, or other activities that can start a fire.
hot work.definition: Hot work includes welding, grinding, cutting, or other activities that can start a fire.
hot work.example: The permit required a fire watch for hot work near stored insulation.

commissioning script.meaning: A commissioning script sets out steps, expected responses, roles, and acceptance criteria for a test.
commissioning script.definition: A commissioning script sets out steps, expected responses, roles, and acceptance criteria for a test.
commissioning script.example: Does the commissioning script meet the acceptance criteria?

system readiness.meaning: System readiness means equipment, documentation, access, and prerequisites are complete enough for commissioning.
system readiness.definition: System readiness means equipment, documentation, access, and prerequisites are complete enough for commissioning.
system readiness.example: The meeting focused on system readiness for the fire alarm cause-and-effect test.

cause and effect matrix.meaning: A cause and effect matrix defines how systems should respond to alarms, signals, or events.
cause and effect matrix.definition: A cause and effect matrix defines how systems should respond to alarms, signals, or events.
cause and effect matrix.example: The fire alarm cause and effect matrix showed that smoke fans should start on detector activation.

defect liability period.meaning: The defect liability period is the post-completion contract period during which the contractor must repair defects at their own cost.
defect liability period.definition: The defect liability period is the post-completion contract period during which the contractor must repair defects at their own cost.
defect liability period.example: Always document any defects found during the defect liability period.

commissioning certificate.meaning: A commissioning certificate records that a system or item has been tested and accepted.
commissioning certificate.definition: A commissioning certificate records that a system or item has been tested and accepted.
commissioning certificate.example: The consultant signed the commissioning certificate for the booster pump set.

performance test.meaning: A performance test checks capacity, efficiency, flow, pressure, or other required operating values.
performance test.definition: A performance test checks capacity, efficiency, flow, pressure, or other required operating values.
performance test.example: The chiller performance test was repeated after sensor calibration.

integrity test.meaning: An integrity test verifies that a system, seal, cable, or enclosure remains intact.
integrity test.definition: An integrity test verifies that a system, seal, cable, or enclosure remains intact.
integrity test.example: The containment integrity test confirmed there were no leaks in the clean agent pipework.

loop test.meaning: A loop test verifies wiring, signal transmission, and response between an instrument and control system.
loop test.definition: A loop test verifies wiring, signal transmission, and response between an instrument and control system.
loop test.example: The BMS contractor completed a loop test for each temperature sensor.

megger test.meaning: A megger test measures insulation resistance in cables or equipment.
megger test.definition: A megger test measures insulation resistance in cables or equipment.
megger test.example: The cable could not be terminated until the megger test passed.

torque test.meaning: A torque test checks whether bolts or terminals are tightened to the specified value.
torque test.definition: A torque test checks whether bolts or terminals are tightened to the specified value.
torque test.example: The QA checklist required a torque test on all busbar bolts.

failover.meaning: Failover is the automatic transfer to backup equipment or paths when the primary system fails.
failover.definition: Failover is the automatic transfer to backup equipment or paths when the primary system fails.
failover.example: The data center performed a failover test from utility power to generator supply.

latency.meaning: Latency is the time delay between a request and a response in a digital system.
latency.definition: Latency is the time delay between a request and a response in a digital system.
latency.example: The operations team investigated high latency between the application and storage network.

patch panel.meaning: A patch panel provides ports where network cables are terminated and cross-connected.
patch panel.definition: A patch panel provides ports where network cables are terminated and cross-connected.
patch panel.example: The technician traced the server connection back to the patch panel.

fiber backbone.meaning: A fiber backbone is the primary fiber-optic cabling linking rooms, floors, or network zones.
fiber backbone.definition: A fiber backbone is the primary fiber-optic cabling linking rooms, floors, or network zones.
fiber backbone.example: The fiber backbone was tested before connecting the new data hall.

cross-connect.meaning: A cross-connect links circuits, equipment, or patching fields in a controlled cabling environment.
cross-connect.definition: A cross-connect links circuits, equipment, or patching fields in a controlled cabling environment.
cross-connect.example: The carrier requested a cross-connect from the meet-me room to the client rack.

white space.meaning: White space is the controlled data center area where racks, servers, and network equipment are installed.
white space.definition: White space is the controlled data center area where racks, servers, and network equipment are installed.
white space.example: The cooling assessment covered all white space zones in the new data hall.

meet-me room.meaning: A meet-me room is a controlled space where telecom carriers and customers connect networks.
meet-me room.definition: A meet-me room is a controlled space where telecom carriers and customers connect networks.
meet-me room.example: The fiber provider handed over the circuit in the meet-me room.

uptime.meaning: Uptime is the period when a system or facility is available and functioning.
uptime.definition: Uptime is the period when a system or facility is available and functioning.
uptime.example: The service agreement required very high uptime for the data center cooling system.

service level agreement.meaning: A service level agreement defines expected service performance, response times, and responsibilities.
service level agreement.definition: A service level agreement defines expected service performance, response times, and responsibilities.
service level agreement.example: The facilities team reviewed the service level agreement after repeated response delays.

nonconformance report.meaning: A nonconformance report records work, material, or process that does not meet approved requirements.
nonconformance report.definition: A nonconformance report records work, material, or process that does not meet approved requirements.
nonconformance report.example: If the NCR is not closed within 30 days, escalate to the project manager.

corrective action.meaning: Corrective action fixes the root cause of a nonconformance or recurring issue.
corrective action.definition: Corrective action fixes the root cause of a nonconformance or recurring issue.
corrective action.example: The corrective action required retraining the team on cable termination procedure.

root cause.meaning: A root cause is the fundamental reason a failure, delay, or defect occurred.
root cause.definition: A root cause is the fundamental reason a failure, delay, or defect occurred.
root cause.example: The investigation found the root cause was an outdated drawing issued to site.

lessons learned.meaning: Lessons learned are practical insights recorded to improve future projects or activities.
lessons learned.definition: Lessons learned are practical insights recorded to improve future projects or activities.
lessons learned.example: The project team documented lessons learned after the commissioning delay.

commercial impact.meaning: Commercial impact is the cost, payment, claim, or contract effect of an event or decision.
commercial impact.definition: Commercial impact is the cost, payment, claim, or contract effect of an event or decision.
commercial impact.example: The delay notice explained the commercial impact of late design approval.

technical clarification.meaning: A technical clarification resolves uncertainty about drawings, specifications, scope, or design intent.
technical clarification.definition: A technical clarification resolves uncertainty about drawings, specifications, scope, or design intent.
technical clarification.example: The contractor raised a technical clarification about the fire alarm interface.

coordination clash.meaning: A coordination clash occurs when two elements need the same space or interfere with each other.
coordination clash.definition: A coordination clash occurs when two elements need the same space or interfere with each other.
coordination clash.example: The BIM review found a coordination clash between the duct and cable ladder.

priority action.meaning: A priority action is an agreed task that needs urgent or early attention.
priority action.definition: A priority action is an agreed task that needs urgent or early attention.
priority action.example: The meeting chair marked the generator fuel issue as a priority action.

open item.meaning: An open item is a task, comment, defect, or question that remains unresolved.
open item.definition: An open item is a task, comment, defect, or question that remains unresolved.
open item.example: The consultant asked for an update on all open items before the progress meeting.

decision log.meaning: A decision log records decisions, dates, owners, and the reasons behind them.
decision log.definition: A decision log records decisions, dates, owners, and the reasons behind them.
decision log.example: The design manager updated the decision log after the client approved the facade color.

action tracker.meaning: An action tracker records tasks, owners, deadlines, and closure status.
action tracker.definition: An action tracker records tasks, owners, deadlines, and closure status.
action tracker.example: The weekly action tracker showed that three submittals were overdue.
